reasoning: Classified product 'steel building structures' under tariff line 73089090 ('Other structures of iron or steel') as the best match.
Tariff line 73089090 is preferential under India-UAE CEPA with a 2026 CEPA rate of 0%.
Tariff schedule lists MFN tariff rate at 15% and effective rate at 10%; CEPA rate is 0%.
Product qualifies under rule CTSH + VA 40% (PSR-IN-R113), satisfying both tariff shift and 45.0% value addition threshold on FOB basis.
Estimated saving of 10000.00 AED calculated on shipment value of 100000.00 AED based on 10% effective MFN reduction.
Mapped step-by-step certificate claim process across factory registration, COO application, issuance, direct consignment, and record keeping.
Gathered applicable caveats regarding effective MFN rates, CIF valuation basis, BCD scope, issuer notes, and free zone eligibility.

classification.description: Other structures of iron or steel

origin_result.basis: Final manufacture takes place in the UAE, manufacturing operations go beyond minimal operations, all 2 non-originating inputs meet the CTSH requirement outside subheading 730890, and value addition reaches 45.0% on an FOB basis against the required 40% threshold.

procedure.step: Before applying for a certificate of origin, the factory must be registered through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade receives applications through the Certificate of Origin for India e-service portal, requiring commercial invoices and factory registration proof.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000.
The competent authority issues the certificate of origin prior to, at, or within 5 working days of export, valid for 12 months.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
The exporter must ensure goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India, indicating third-party invoicing on the certificate if applicable.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, keeping records for at least 5 years; electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit.
The exporter must keep origin records, including cost breakdowns, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The tariff schedule prints 15%, but an exemption notification lowers the duty actually charged to 10%; the effective rate is used.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
